messages:
Jamie L: Heads up — tracing costs spiked this week after the new billing dashboard queries started pulling full traces for high-traffic routes. Thinking we should try a TTL + head/tail hybrid instead of current 1-in-N sampling by route.
Ravi K: Ugh. Do you have numbers?
Jamie L: Quick: traces ingested up ~42% month-on-month, storage burn on our long-tail spans is main driver. Tail traces (errors/slow) are small fraction but we keep full context for everything.
Sophia: 42% is scary. Proposal?
Jamie L: Proposal: keep full spans for head (first X spans per trace or first Y ms) for all routes, then for long-running traces apply tail-preserve for error/slow requests, and TTL older than 7 days for low-tier customers. Also dynamic bucketization by route: routes with > p95 latency or high error rate get higher tail retention.
Leo: So head = prefix traces, tail = suffix around the abnormal events, TTL = eviction. How do we delta-apply this to existing OTel pipeline without huge churn?
Jamie L: Minimal change to pipeline: exporter side adds a sampling decision attribute on spans, downstream collector has small policy plugin that filters/marks spans for retention. No changes to trace model.
Maria P: Can we express this with existing otel config? Something like a pipeline processor?
Jamie L: Exactly. Example draft config:
```
processors:
  headtail_sampler:
    head_spans: 8
    head_time_ms: 50
    tail_window_ms: 2000
    error_keep: true
    per_route_overrides:
      "/api/generate": { tail_window_ms: 5000, head_spans: 16 }
exporters:
  redwood_storage:
    retention_policy_from: span.attributes._sampling_decision
```
Ravi K: I like per_route overrides. We also need per-customer tier (free/dev/prod) — retention costs should map to billing.
Sophia: For privacy/compliance we must ensure PII spans are dropped earlier for some customers. That suggests an ordering: first PII scrubber, then sampling policy, then exporter.
Jamie L: Good catch. Enforcement order: scrubber -> sampling decision -> exporter. Also add a small audit attribute to retained traces so billing and compliance teams can audit retention reasons.
otel-bot: Incoming config check: headtail_sampler: head_spans must be <= 128; tail_window_ms recommended <= 10000.
Leo: How about routing policy for low-latency SLO routes? We can't add extra processing latency in the hot path. Sampler must be async or constant-time.
Jamie L: Plan: sampling decision is made in the collector hot path but only reading route metadata + short histogram counters (lock-free). Heavy work (prefix caching, kv-store writes) happens async to exporter.
Maria P: What about queryability — if we drop spans, dashboards might lose heatmaps. Maybe we keep a lightweight summary span (synthetic parent) for dropped sections so observability still shows fullness.
Ravi K: That helps UX. But we need to ensure storage ops don't explode with synthetic spans. Maybe summaries are aggregated per minute per route.
Sophia: Also consider tail-sampling amplification: if we rely on span attributes (error=true) we need to be sure downstream services propagate status consistently. Otherwise we miss tails.
Leo: Could add a short-lived cache of suspicious trace IDs from the sampler so later spans are retroactively flagged for retention (up to some window). Tradeoff: memory + complexity.
Jamie L: Yes — weak cache with eviction TTL e.g., 30s. If later spans show error, we mark earlier spans for retention (async index).
ops-bot: Alert: exporters are rate-limited at 120r/s per region. If we increase async retention writes, we need quota tuning.
Maria P: Which leads to rollout plan: start with a single low-traffic route and dev-tier customers for 2 weeks, measure retention delta and query impact, then ramp.
Ravi K: Need metrics: traces ingested/sec, bytes/day, %traces with synthetic-summary, per-route retention ratio, billing delta per tier.
Sophia: Tests: unit tests for sampler logic, canary with replayed traffic, and a backfill job to re-evaluate recent traces for missed tails.
Jamie L: I'll draft a PR for a collector processor with the config above + telemetry metrics. Who wants to review the design doc?
Leo: I'll take the perf section and async design.
Maria P: I'll own compliance + audit attributes.
Ravi K: I'll do billing mapping/metrics.
Sophia: I'll write tests + canary plan.
Jamie L: Thanks — I'll post the doc and link to a short replay script. Expect initial PoC in ~6d. :thumbsup:
otel-bot: Config lint OK for current schema.
Maria P: small nit — add an opt-out for customers who want raw traces forever (enterprise).
Jamie L: Good call, add enterprise retention flag.
Ravi K: Sounds good. If anyone has empirical thresholds (head_spans, tail_window_ms) from other systems, drop them here.
Leo: I'll dig up historical p95/p99 distributions and propose defaults.
Jamie L: Perfect — will keep thread updated.
